Title: Redis-backed caching for slow backend reads, starting with Friends overview
Category: backend

get-spec output:
Switching from Profile to Friends (and likely other reads) is slow every time -- there is currently zero caching on backend read endpoints. friends_overview (backend/users/friends.py) runs three uncached DB queries on every call. The infrastructure for Redis already exists and is unused for this: backend/backend/settings.py wires Django CACHES with a three-tier fallback (Redis via REDIS_URL, else shared DatabaseCache, else local LocMemCache), redis is already in requirements.txt, and backend/users/leaderboard.py has its own separate direct-redis-client pattern for sorted-set ranking only. Task: 1) Research and pick the best-fit managed Redis provider for this stack (Vercel serverless Django + Supabase Postgres already using a transaction pooler due to IPv6/connection issues, see docs/DEPLOYMENT.md) -- weigh HTTP/REST-based options that avoid persistent-connection problems in serverless, not just the cheapest choice. Document exact setup steps (account, env var names, region) in docs/DEPLOYMENT.md but do NOT create the account or spend money -- the owner adds real credentials afterward. 2) Using the existing Django CACHES abstraction (not the leaderboard raw-client pattern), add caching to friends_overview and audit other slow, frequently-repeated reads across trivia/ and users/ for the same treatment, with correct invalidation (e.g. friends_overview must invalidate immediately on a friend/request/block action for the affected users, not just time out). 3) Must work correctly with zero Redis configured today (falls back to DatabaseCache). This is an infrastructure-level, multi-endpoint change -- treat as needing a real design pass, not a single-file patch.

## 2026-09-29 — Redis-backed read caching (friends_overview first): risk low vs high, sonnet vs opus
Context: backend card, no override. The spec asks for three things: research a managed Redis
provider and document it in DEPLOYMENT.md (no account, no spend); add read caching on the existing
Django `CACHES` tiers (`settings.py`: Redis, then DatabaseCache, then LocMem), starting with
`users/friends.py::friends_overview`, and audit other reads in trivia/ and users/; and invalidate
straight away on friend, request and block actions. It must also work with no Redis configured.
`difficulty: hard` was clear: this is the first read-cache pattern in the app, it spans several
endpoints, and the spec itself asks for a design pass. The close calls were the other two picks.
(1) Risk. `high` was defensible: a per-user cache key that is wrong or stale can show one user's
friends or requests to another, or keep showing a user who was just blocked. The same `CACHES`
also holds the throttle counters (`backend/throttles.py`), and those are abuse protection.
(2) Engine. `sonnet` was defensible because the design round can reduce the work to explicit steps:
key scheme, TTL, an invalidation hook for each mutating view, and tests for each.
Decision: `risk: low`. The card touches none of the risk-high triggers: auth, the data pipeline,
multiplayer protocol or a protected path. It is a performance change, not security work. The
data-leak and blocked-user concerns become acceptance criteria in the design round (keys scoped by
user id, invalidation tests for every mutation, and a test that a block drops the blocked user
straight away). The plan must not change the throttle cache config. `engineModel: opus`
(provisional), because the rubric says a hard task implemented from a plan goes to opus, and
getting invalidation complete across every friend mutation is judgment. `planModel: fable`.
Consequences: the design round should re-pick per step. The DEPLOYMENT.md provider write-up and
the mechanical per-endpoint wrapping can go to sonnet once the key and invalidation scheme is
fixed. If the plan changes `CACHES`/`settings.py` behaviour, meaning throttle storage, raise the
card to `risk: high`.
